summary: Changelog records fixes for triple-click around inline links, DOM range normalization for Firefox, and selection adjustment after triple-click.
DOM range import sets model anchor/focus then normalizes because Firefox can use element points; triple-click is a DOM-selection import trigger.
Triple-click over-selection is corrected to the intended parent block when focus leaks into another node.
Link transform logic saves/restores selection and normalizes final boundary points.
Classic Slate treats triple-click hanging ranges as an editor-level range correction concern.
Visual-native inline triple-click row now runs on all desktop engines with normalized selected text, model endpoint assertion, no-double-highlight assertion, and screenshot artifact.
